purpose: Evidence-backed candidate mapping only; not a certification or compliance assertion.

controls.title: Attach a Web Application Firewall to Internet-Facing Listeners

requirements.requirement: When a listener is internet-facing and serves HTTP or HTTPS traffic, a web application firewall policy MUST be associated with it.
requirements.scope: A standalone Envoy proxy-Wasm WAF fixture inspected harmless requests; no internet-facing TraderX listener or State 019 gateway is covered.
requirements.limitation: A local WAF fixture is not a deployed listener association or a managed-cloud control.

requirements.requirement: When a web application firewall policy is associated with a listener, the policy MUST run in blocking (prevention) mode rather than detection-only mode.
requirements.scope: The fixture compared Off, DetectionOnly and On; benign requests succeeded and suspicious requests were rejected before the recording backend in On mode.
requirements.limitation: This proves behavior only in the standalone fixture. It does not prove deployed WAF coverage, a successful exploit in Off mode, or integration with Envoy Gateway.

requirements.requirement: When a user workload namespace is created, an enforced network policy MUST deny all ingress and egress traffic by default.
requirements.scope: A dedicated local kind cluster applied default-deny ingress and egress in the isolated probe namespace; an unrelated client was denied while a positive-control client remained connected.
requirements.limitation: This is a live local-cluster probe, not a managed-cloud cluster or full State 019 workload network-policy acceptance.

requirements.requirement: When communication is required, each allow policy MUST identify the approved source, destination, protocol, and port using stable namespace, workload, or network selectors.
requirements.scope: The probe's allow policies selected the approved client/server workloads and TCP port 8080; the positive and negative probes ran against the local Cilium data plane.
requirements.limitation: The fixture tests one explicit flow, not every State 019 service edge. Ingress/mesh comparison remains future work.

controls.title: Enforce Least Privilege Within the Database

requirements.requirement: When a database login is used by an application, that login MUST NOT hold an administrative or superuser role.
requirements.scope: Four PostgreSQL application logins in the dedicated local kind lab were checked for superuser/admin flags, memberships, ownership and effective grants.
requirements.limitation: The committed SQL campaign is local-cluster evidence, not a managed database service assessment. The State 019 processor HTTP evidence is a separate component candidate, not deployment evidence.

requirements.requirement: When privileges are granted on a schema or table, the grant MUST NOT be made to the engine's public or every-login role.
requirements.scope: The SQL permission compiler revokes database, schema, table and sequence privileges from PUBLIC; the local campaign verifies service-role grants and denied out-of-scope operations.
requirements.limitation: This checks the tested PostgreSQL fixture only. It does not establish authorization within legitimate service grants, managed-cloud controls, or State 019's unfinished full execution cutover.

controls.title: Detect Suspicious Workload Runtime Activity
controls.catalog_version: unreleased main snapshot at 00bb0a8ffb8c6894968d25e46e0bbe03f14c3919 (no versioned release verified)
controls.test_command: Not run: no runtime detection engine has been selected or integrated.

requirements.requirement: When a cluster is operational, runtime threat detection MUST be enabled for its nodes and workloads and MUST alert an authorized security function on suspicious container activity.
requirements.scope: State 019 FR-019-05 and task S019-08 plan a bounded comparison of one runtime engine in observation and enforcement modes.
requirements.limitation: The requirement is present in the pinned FINOS main snapshot but not in the checked v2026.11 Kubernetes release. No runtime sensor, alert delivery, detection or prevention result is evidenced.

requirements.requirement: When a workload is admitted to a user workload namespace, it MUST satisfy the Kubernetes Baseline Pod Security Standard.
requirements.scope: Committed probes show admission denials for privileged and host-access workloads in the dedicated local cluster; selected C3 workloads were separately verified.
requirements.limitation: Evidence covers the named local lab namespaces and workloads, not every namespace or a managed cluster.

requirements.requirement: When a Linux workload is admitted to a user workload namespace, it MUST satisfy the Kubernetes Restricted Pod Security Standard.
requirements.scope: Restricted admission rejected a non-conforming probe; selected business and collector workloads were checked for non-root, seccomp, dropped capabilities, token suppression and related settings.
requirements.limitation: The probes do not establish universal policy coverage or runtime prevention of misuse of allowed database or broker access.

controls.title: Admit Only Trusted Container Images
controls.test_command: No admission test for approved registry, signature/provenance verification, or critical-vulnerability rejection is recorded.

requirements.requirement: When a workload is admitted, every container image MUST originate from an approved registry AND be referenced by an immutable digest.
requirements.scope: Committed workload evidence records digest-pinned images for tested services; admission enforcement of an approved registry is not established.
requirements.limitation: Digest pinning alone does not establish approved-registry policy, signature verification, provenance, or that every admitted image is covered.

requirements.requirement: When a container image is admitted, its signature and provenance attestation MUST be verified against an approved publisher and build process.
requirements.scope: Approved-image admission remains a State 019 security integration gate.
requirements.limitation: No committed signature/provenance admission test or evidence was found.

requirements.requirement: When a container image contains a known critical vulnerability, admission of that image MUST be denied.
requirements.scope: Image vulnerability admission remains a State 019 security integration gate.
requirements.limitation: No committed critical-vulnerability policy or admission result was found.

controls.title: Restrict External Exposure of Workload Services
controls.test_command: Not run: no approved ingress/gateway integration or external-exposure policy comparison is implemented.

requirements.requirement: When a LoadBalancer Service, Ingress, or Gateway is created, its load balancer MUST be provisioned with internal scope unless its namespace is approved for external exposure.
requirements.scope: State 019 gateway/WAF integration and the later ingress comparison remain open.
requirements.limitation: No Kubernetes LoadBalancer, Ingress or Gateway exposure policy result is committed.

requirements.requirement: When an externally scoped load balancer is created for a workload, it MUST restrict inbound traffic to an approved source address allowlist.
requirements.scope: No externally scoped workload load balancer is assessed.
requirements.limitation: The WAF fixture is not deployed coverage and does not prove a managed load-balancer source allowlist.

requirements.requirement: When a Service is created or updated, it MUST NOT set external IP addresses unless they are explicitly approved.
requirements.scope: No service admission rule for external IPs is evidenced.
requirements.limitation: No positive/negative Service admission test is committed.

requirements.requirement: When a Service is created in a user workload namespace, it MUST NOT be of type NodePort.
requirements.scope: No NodePort admission rule is evidenced.
requirements.limitation: No positive/negative NodePort admission test is committed.

requirements.requirement: When a user or group is granted cluster access, each cloud access binding and Kubernetes role binding MUST grant only an approved role required by that identity's documented responsibilities.
requirements.scope: The evidence checks selected service and collector identities, not a cluster-wide inventory of human/cloud bindings and their approved responsibilities.
requirements.limitation: No complete role/binding inventory or documented responsibility-to-entitlement review is committed.

requirements.requirement: When a non-system Kubernetes role is defined, it MUST NOT grant wildcard verbs, wildcard resources, or wildcard API groups.
requirements.scope: No cluster-wide non-system role audit is recorded.
requirements.limitation: Collector RBAC checks do not prove all roles are free of wildcard grants.

requirements.requirement: When a non-system RoleBinding or ClusterRoleBinding is created or updated, its subjects MUST NOT include the system:anonymous, system:unauthenticated, or system:authenticated groups.
requirements.scope: No binding admission or cluster-wide subject inventory is recorded.
requirements.limitation: No positive/negative binding test is committed.

requirements.requirement: When a non-system Kubernetes role grants the escalate, bind, or impersonate verbs, or grants approve on certificatesigningrequests/approval, that role MUST be bound only to a dedicated administrative group.
requirements.scope: No cluster-wide privileged-verb or certificate-approval role assessment is recorded.
requirements.limitation: No role-binding evidence covers these administrative permissions.

requirements.requirement: When a workload does not call the Kubernetes API, its service account token MUST NOT be mounted into the workload.
requirements.scope: The tested business workloads and collector configuration suppress service-account tokens; committed live workload evidence confirms token absence for selected pods.
requirements.limitation: This is a selected local-lab workload check, not an inventory of every cluster workload or a managed-cloud assessment.

requirements.requirement: When a non-system Kubernetes role grants create on pods or workload controllers in a system or privileged namespace, or create on pods/exec, pods/attach, pods/portforward, pods/proxy, services/proxy, nodes/proxy, or serviceaccounts/token, or update or patch on pods/ephemeralcontainers, in any namespace, that role MUST be bound only to a dedicated administrative group.
requirements.scope: No cluster-wide privileged workload/API subresource permission review is recorded.
requirements.limitation: Scoped application and collector checks do not establish this administrative-role requirement.

requirements.requirement: When a secret is mounted or injected into a workload, it MUST be readable only by the intended workload's service account.
requirements.scope: Selected C3 workload tests deny cross-service secret reads and use dedicated SQL Secret references.
requirements.limitation: Evidence is limited to tested workloads and secrets; no cluster-wide secret-access review or managed secret-store proof is available.

requirements.requirement: When Kubernetes secret access is granted, workload roles MUST be limited to the required named secrets and MUST NOT grant unrestricted list or watch access.
requirements.scope: Workload service accounts have no RBAC grants in the tested slice; the isolated collector's scoped RBAC was checked separately.
requirements.limitation: The committed checks do not inventory every cluster role or secret grant.

requirements.requirement: When a Kubernetes Secret is persisted to the cluster datastore, it MUST be envelope-encrypted with a key held in a cloud key management service.
requirements.scope: The local kind cluster has no assessed cloud KMS envelope-encryption configuration.
requirements.limitation: No managed-cloud KMS evidence is committed; local private-file credential storage does not satisfy this Kubernetes datastore requirement.

requirements.requirement: When a workload is deployed, secret values MUST NOT be present in its container images, ConfigMaps, or plain environment variables in the workload specification.
requirements.scope: Database identity checks reject tested literal/cross-service credentials and verify SQL password Secret references.
requirements.limitation: The check is scoped to the tested SQL deployment inputs; it is not a scan of all images, ConfigMaps, manifests or workloads.

requirements.requirement: When a cluster is operational, long-lived service-account-token Secrets MUST NOT exist outside an approved exception list.
requirements.scope: Selected workload pods have no mounted service-account token.
requirements.limitation: No cluster-wide inventory of legacy service-account-token Secret objects or approved exceptions is committed.

controls.title: Preserve Kubernetes Audit and Monitoring Records

requirements.requirement: When a cluster is operational, Kubernetes API audit logs, control-plane logs, and security-relevant node, workload, and network activity records MUST be enabled and exported to an approved external logging destination.
requirements.scope: Committed local-cluster evidence confirms selected application logs, metrics and traces persist across telemetry pod recreation.
requirements.limitation: It does not establish Kubernetes API audit/control-plane logging or export to an independently governed external destination.

requirements.requirement: When Kubernetes audit or monitoring records are retained, write, delete, and configuration access MUST be separated from cluster workload and routine cluster administration identities.
requirements.scope: The collector has a separate constrained identity and selected RBAC/admission boundaries were verified.
requirements.limitation: Evidence does not prove independent write/delete/configuration custody or tamper-resistant retention; local telemetry stores and private checkpoints remain in the lab boundary.

requirements.requirement: When a cluster-admin binding, an admission webhook or policy object, or the audit log category configuration changes, the monitoring system MUST generate an alert for review by an authorized security function.
requirements.scope: No committed detection and alert-delivery test covers these Kubernetes configuration changes.
requirements.limitation: Telemetry availability is not evidence that these security change alerts exist.

requirements.requirement: When cluster or workload metrics are exposed or exported, read access MUST be restricted to authorized monitoring identities.
requirements.scope: The evidence verifies metric persistence but not access restrictions for every cluster/workload metric endpoint.
requirements.limitation: No complete metrics authorization test is committed.

requirements.requirement: When a cluster is operational, runtime threat detection MUST be enabled for its nodes and workloads and MUST alert an authorized security function on suspicious container activity.
requirements.scope: The v2026.11 catalog includes this runtime-detection requirement; State 019 FR-019-05 plans later observation/enforcement comparison.
requirements.limitation: No runtime sensor or alert-delivery evidence is committed. Detection after an effect is not prevention.

interpretation_notes: A local fixture, component candidate, or deployed local kind cluster is not a managed-cloud approximation unless explicitly described as such; no managed-cloud approximation is claimed in this assessment.

CCC.K8S.CN23 is present at the pinned FINOS main commit but absent from the checked orchestration/k8s/v2026.11 release. The released catalog has a related runtime-detection requirement at CCC.K8S.CN14.AR05.
State 019 HTTP authorization tests and synthetic-token checks are component evidence only. They are not NATS subject authorization, deployment TLS, or deployment-trust evidence.
Runtime detection and runtime prevention are separate outcomes. No runtime detection engine or prevention result is claimed.
Ingress and service-mesh profiles and the CALM comparison are future work as described by system/platform-control-comparison.md; they are not current implementation evidence.
